title: Posted Notice: Elevation Allowance on Loads Received Away From the Contracted Facility
content:
Where grain sold under Grain Marketing Contracts is received at a facility other than the one the contract calls for, the cooperative takes an elevation allowance for moving it. The allowance is a percentage of the net bushels those loads carry, and it is taken off those bushels before they are credited to the contract.

**The allowance posted.**

- Where two or more loads were received at a facility other than the one the contract calls for and the bushels they carry reach 2500 bushels, the allowance is the terminal elevation allowance of 1.2 percent.
- Where loads were received at a facility other than the one the contract calls for, but not two or more of them carrying that many bushels, the allowance is the single-haul allowance of 0.6 percent.
- Where no load was received at any other facility, no elevation allowance is taken.

## Both sides of the parcel size

The terminal allowance asks for the two conditions together. Two loads carrying 2500 net bushels between them reach the parcel size and take 1.2 percent, the figure itself qualifying. Two loads carrying 2,499 bushels between them fall short and take 0.6 percent, and so does a single load of 4,000 bushels, since one load is not two.

## Illustration on hypothetical loads

Three loads received at another facility carry 3,600 net bushels between them. The allowance is 1.2 percent, being 43.20 bushels, and 3,556.80 bushels are credited. Had those same 3,600 bushels arrived on a single load, the allowance would be 0.6 percent, being 21.60 bushels, and 3,578.40 bushels would be credited.
